discussion_comments.comment_body: This one doesn't hold. Without `-m`, `git read-tree <tree1> <tree2>` reads both trees into stage 0; it only fails if they share a path, and a checkpoint's tracked tree and its untracked-files parent never do. Repro on git 2.43: read-tree of a tree with `a.ts` and a tree with `new.ts` gives `100644 ... 0 a.ts` and `100644 ... 0 new.ts`, and `write-tree` succeeds. The path is also covered by `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts`, whose checkpoints carry an untracked third parent (including an agent-created `new.ts`), and by a manual run where agent-created untracked files showed up in Last turn and Session.

Fixed in 2c1a7f7d7: normalization now recurses into `items` (object and tuple forms) and into `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches before the object-likeness gate, so nested uppercase types lowercase at every depth. Covered by the new "normalizes nested array items and combinator branches" test.

Fair point. Switched to splitting on `path.sep` only (same approach as the SDK's workspace file-indexer), so POSIX filenames containing a literal backslash are left intact. Added a POSIX-only test for that case.
